findings.title: State-changing unsubscribe action is a GET route without CSRF/token
findings.body: The unsubscribe action changes TopicUser.notification_level in response to a GET request and skips XHR checks. Rails CSRF protection does not apply to GET, so any logged-in user visiting a malicious page could have topics silently muted or downgraded by an image or link to /t/:topic_id/unsubscribe. Email unsubscribe links should use a signed one-time key or a POST route.

findings.title: Unsubscribe crashes when no TopicUser row exists
findings.body: TopicsController#unsubscribe does `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` and then dereferences `tu.notification_level`. For users without an existing topic_users row for the topic, `tu` is nil and the action raises NoMethodError. The action should create or update the row, for example via TopicUser.change or find_or_create_by.

findings.title: Direct TopicUser#save! bypasses notification-level bookkeeping
findings.body: The unsubscribe action mutates notification_level with `tu.save!` instead of `TopicUser.change`. This skips setting notifications_changed_at and notifications_reason_id and does not publish the MessageBus level-change event. Leaving notifications_reason_id nil can allow later automatic tracking to override the user's mute, and open clients will not receive the state change.

findings.title: Global unsubscribe_link now requires unsubscribe_url for all callers
findings.body: The `unsubscribe_link` translation was changed to interpolate `%{unsubscribe_url}`, but Email::MessageBuilder only has that value when the caller passes `unsubscribe_url`. Only `send_notification_email` was updated. Any other email or plugin that builds with `add_unsubscribe_link: true` but omits `unsubscribe_url` will raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument and fail to send.

findings.title: track_visit! uses topic id as user_id when passed ids
findings.body: In `TopicUser.track_visit!`, `user_id = user.is_a?(User) ? user.id : topic` falls back to the `topic` argument rather than the `user` argument when the second argument is not a User object. TopicsController calls this with integer topic_id/user_id, so it can create or update topic_users rows with user_id equal to the topic_id, corrupting per-user topic state. The fallback should be `user`.

findings.title: Spec does not assert the new unsubscribe_url is included
findings.body: The updated spec passes `unsubscribe_url` to Email::MessageBuilder but only asserts that the body contains `user_preferences_url`. It never checks that the new per-topic unsubscribe URL appears in the body or HTML, so the new interpolation/link behavior is untested.
